curated-fs-khand-gf-mate-sc: Crisp Khand tucks its letters close, with no heavy-to-light shifts. Mate SC, a classic serif, brings faint nib-pressure variation to its round letters, so the page moves from uniform strokes to softly pressured ones.
curated-fs-khand-gf-noto-serif-hk: Contemporary Khand reads like signage, plain in every line weight. Khand is best at crisp, tight headlines, while Noto Serif HK offers gentle pen-like modulation in its bowls and generous gaps where curves end.
curated-fs-khand-gf-old-standard-tt: Khand lays down a plain stripe of constant ink. Old Standard TT, a classic serif, is built of heavy pillars and fine wires that nearly vanish, so it's better with brief text than long.
curated-fs-khand-gf-rufina: Bookish Rufina brings fat vertical strokes and filament-thin connectors. Khand, drawn like bent wire, holds steady beside Rufina's high-contrast strokes, and the serif is happiest on a short visit.
curated-fs-khand-gf-sedan: Round letters drawn like bent wire give Khand its look. Sedan, a classic serif, adds a mellow range of stroke weights and terminals held far from the stroke body, so the page gets both wire and warmth.
curated-fs-khand-gf-sura: Sharp and spare, Khand draws a line that never swells or tapers. Sura, a serif, thins its bowls gracefully but not sharply, with slightly thinner hairlines and terminals that never close in.
curated-fs-kohinoor-zerone-gf-frank-ruhl: Kohinoor Zerone draws round letters like bent wire, its o equally heavy on the sides and across the top. Frank Ruhl Libre, a serif, has razor-fine joins; skip long paragraphs.
curated-fs-kohinoor-zerone-gf-kaisei-har: Horizontals no thinner than verticals give Kohinoor Zerone a precise look, right for a photographer signature mark. And Kaisei HarunoUmi, a text serif, is made for brief reading, with fat bars, fine threads and cupped bowls.
curated-fs-kola-dm-sans: Kola is best at bold, plain statements up top. DM Sans does the friendly part, with wide-set terminals on its s, and is better with short lines than long paragraphs.
curated-fs-kola-gf-noto-sans-old-south-a: Distinctive Kola keeps its display letters plain and bold. Noto Sans Old South Arabian is the approachable, clean one, with curved strokes that stop before turning inward, and it's best on short text.
